As these immigrants come into your country, you start feeling that your quality of life is worsening, finding it harder to afford basics like rent and food.

It's getting harder for you to support your family. In Canada over the past five years, there has been a massive influx of immigrants, causing housing prices to skyrocket. The United States, with its larger economy, has more stable housing prices; young people can still afford to buy houses there, unlike in Canada where housing prices are now unaffordable.

In Canada, GDP is growing, but housing prices are surging, making the Canadian dream of owning a home essentially dead. There's an interesting anomaly: as immigration increases, housing supply isn't rising proportionally. This might be because policymakers prioritize profits from real estate over public welfare. Real estate developers can make more money with higher demand and limited supply, driving up property values and benefiting existing homeowners at the expense of new immigrants.

Another issue in Western countries is that native populations are not having children. In Canada, the birth rate is steadily declining, while immigration provides most of the new population. Currently, 25% of Canadians are first-generation immigrants, and this trend will lead to a significant shift in demographics within the next few decades, causing considerable conflict and tension in the country.
